The **2023–24 [Futbol Club Barcelona](FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") season** is the club's [124th season in existence](List_of_FC_Barcelona_seasons "List of FC Barcelona seasons") and their [93rd consecutive season](La_Liga_records_and_statistics#All-time_table "La Liga records and statistics") in the top flight. In addition to the [domestic league](2023%E2%80%9324_La_Liga "2023–24 La Liga"), Barcelona will participate in this season's editions of the [Copa del Rey](2023%E2%80%9324_Copa_del_Rey "2023–24 Copa del Rey"), the [Supercopa de España](2023%E2%80%9324_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2023–24 Supercopa de España"), and the [UEFA Champions League](2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") (entering for the [20th consecutive season](FC_Barcelona_in_international_football#European_Cup_/_Champions_League "FC Barcelona in international football")). The season covers the period from 1 July 2023 until 30 June 2024.

Barcelona will play their official home matches for the entire season at the [Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys](Estadi_Ol%C3%ADmpic_Llu%C3%ADs_Companys "Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys") due to the start of *Espai Barça* project to revamp the club's sporting facilities.[[1]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-1)

This season is the first without captain [Sergio Busquets](Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets"), who left the club after 18 years (15 years as a first team player since the [2008–09 season](2008%E2%80%9309_FC_Barcelona_season "2008–09 FC Barcelona season")) as a free agent in the summer.[[2]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-Sergio-2) It is also the first season since [2011–12](2011%E2%80%9312_FC_Barcelona_season "2011–12 FC Barcelona season") without the left-back [Jordi Alba](Jordi_Alba "Jordi Alba"), who reached an agreement with the club to terminate his contract one year before its expiration.[[3]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-Alba-3)[[4]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-4)

The crest includes a semi-transparent diamond, inspired by the logo of the team who played [the first ever Barça women's football match](Selecci%C3%B3_Barcelona_0%E2%80%930_UE_Centelles "Selecció Barcelona 0–0 UE Centelles") at the [Camp Nou](Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") in 1970.[[5]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-5)
2. [↑](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_ref-awayjersey_8-0) The away kit is predominantly white, inspired by a kit worn by [Johan Cruyff](Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff") in the 1970s. The crest is that used in 1978.[[6]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-7)
3. [↑](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_ref-thirdjersey_10-0) The third kit is intended as a visual metaphor of the "Barça DNA". Using traditional Barça away aqua blue, a weave pattern in blaugrana evokes DNA. Barça DNA is the history, playing style, and development of young talent at the club.[[7]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-9)

## Season overview

### Pre-season

On 8 June 2023, Barcelona announced that the pre-season will start with the players medical examinations on 10 July.[[10]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-14)[[11]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-15)

### August

On 13 August, Barcelona were held to a goalless draw by [Getafe CF](Getafe_CF "Getafe CF") at the Coliseum Alfonso Perez. In an extremely physical match, both teams were reduced to ten men when <Raphinha> and Jamie Mata were sent off in the 42nd and 57th minutes respectively. The match ended with late drama when Barcelona were denied a penalty for a foul on Ronald Araujo right at the end.[[12]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-16)

On 20 August, Barcelona got their first win of the season, winning 2–0 against [Cádiz](C%C3%A1diz_CF "Cádiz CF"), with the goals coming from <Pedri> and [Ferran Torres](Ferran_Torres "Ferran Torres").[[13]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-17)[[14]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-18)

On 27 August, Barcelona defeated [Villarreal](Villarreal_CF "Villarreal CF") 4–3 in a seven-goal thriller. [Gavi](Gavi_(footballer) "Gavi (footballer)"), [Frenkie de Jong](Frenkie_de_Jong "Frenkie de Jong") and Ferran Torres scored a goal each, along with [Robert Lewandowski](Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") who scored his first goal of the season and sealed the win in the 71st minute.[[15]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-19)[[16]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-20)

On 31 August, the draw for the [2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage](2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage "2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage") was held at the [Grimaldi Forum](Grimaldi_Forum "Grimaldi Forum") in <Monaco>. Barcelona was drawn into [Group H](2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_H "2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage"), alongside its opponents [Porto](FC_Porto "FC Porto"), [Shakhtar Donetsk](FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") and debutants [Royal Antwerp](Royal_Antwerp_F.C. "Royal Antwerp F.C.").[[17]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-21)[[18]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-22)[[19]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-23)

### September

On 1 September, Barcelona confirmed the signings of forward [João Félix](Jo%C3%A3o_F%C3%A9lix "João Félix") and defender [João Cancelo](Jo%C3%A3o_Cancelo "João Cancelo") on loan until the end of the season.[[20]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-:0-24)[[21]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-:1-25) On the same day the club also announced that they had sold [Abde Ezzalzouli](Abde_Ezzalzouli "Abde Ezzalzouli") to [Real Betis](Real_Betis "Real Betis") for €7,500,000, and confirmed that they had loaned out three players until the end of the season: [Clément Lenglet](Cl%C3%A9ment_Lenglet "Clément Lenglet") to [Aston Villa](Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C."),[[22]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-:2-26) [Ansu Fati](Ansu_Fati "Ansu Fati") to [Brighton & Hove Albion](Brighton_%26_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.")[[23]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-:3-27) and [Eric García](Eric_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer%2C_born_2001) "Eric García (footballer, born 2001)") to [Girona](Girona_FC "Girona FC").[[24]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-:4-28)

On 3 September, the team got a hard-fought 2–1 away win against [Osasuna](CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna"), with [Jules Koundé](Jules_Kound%C3%A9 "Jules Koundé") and Robert Lewandowski scoring the goals. New signings João Félix, João Cancelo and Iñigo Martínez made their debuts during the match.[[25]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-29)[[26]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-30) [Gavi](Gavi_(footballer) "Gavi (footballer)") made his 100th appearance for Barcelona, thus becoming the youngest Barça player ever to become a centenarian, reaching the figure at the age of 19 years and 27 days.[[27]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-31)[[28]](2023%E2%80%9324_FC_Barcelona_season#cite_note-32)

**Jules Olivier Koundé** ( French pronunciation: [ʒyl ɔlivje kunde]; born 12 November 1998) is a French professional [footballer](Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [centre-back](Centre-back "Centre-back") or [right-back](Right-back "Right-back") for [La Liga](La_Liga "La Liga") club [Barcelona](FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") and the [France national team](France_national_football_team "France national football team").

## Club career

### Bordeaux

Koundé started in his first team debut for [Bordeaux](FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux "FC Girondins de Bordeaux") in the 2–1 [Coupe de France](2017%E2%80%9318_Coupe_de_France "2017–18 Coupe de France") away loss to [US Granville](US_Granville "US Granville") in the round of 64 on 7 January 2018, playing the full 90 minutes of normal time and the full 30 minutes of extra time.[[3]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-soccerway1-3) He started in his [Ligue 1](Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") debut for Bordeaux in a 1–0 away win over [Troyes](Troyes_AC "Troyes AC") on 13 January 2018.[[4]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-4) On 10 February 2018, Koundé scored the opening goal of a 3–2 Ligue 1 home win over [Amiens](Amiens_SC "Amiens SC"); it was his first career Ligue 1 goal and his first competitive goal for Bordeaux's first team.[[5]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-5)

### Sevilla

On 3 July 2019, he signed for Spanish club [Sevilla](Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"). The transfer fee paid to Bordeaux was reported as €25 million.[[6]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-6) In his first season at Sevilla, he helped the club win the [UEFA Europa League](2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Europa_League "2019–20 UEFA Europa League") for a record sixth time and was named in the competition's team of the season.[[7]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-UELW-7)[[8]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-UELTOS-8)

### Barcelona

On 29 July 2022, [Barcelona](FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") announced an agreement with Sevilla for the transfer of Koundé.[[9]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-9) Koundé missed Barcelona's first match of the [La Liga](2022%E2%80%9323_La_Liga "2022–23 La Liga") season against [Rayo Vallecano](Rayo_Vallecano "Rayo Vallecano") as the club could not register him as they were over the league's salary cap limit.[[10]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-10) He also missed Barcelona's second league match against [Real Sociedad](Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad") on 21 August for the same reason.[[11]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-11) Kounde was registered with La Liga on 26 August[[12]](Jules_Kound%C3%A9#cite_note-12) and made his official debut for the club two days later in a 4–0 w

You are a helpful assistant. Current date: 11-20-2023.

# Multi-Agent Delegation

When the user asks a complex question, do not attempt to answer it yourself. Break it up into smaller pieces, then use the `fork` tool to delegate each piece to a subagent. You MUST use the `join` tool to retrieve the subagent's result for each subagent you create with `fork`. Each subagent has access to the exact same tools that you do.

If you are confident you can answer the user's query without help, do not use the delegation tools.

## Writing Instructions

The instructions you give to each subagent SHOULD be a smaller piece of the instructions you were given. Do not delegate your full task to a subagent. Subagents do not have access to the information you have retrieved in prior turns or your thoughts. You must provide each subagent with the necessary context it needs in its instructions.

Your instructions to a subagent can be long, up to about 5000 characters. Each subagent is as capable as you are, but starts with a blank slate, so you must provide it specific and detailed information in its instructions.

Examples of poor instructions:
- Analyze the retrieved page to find the number of stations.
- Implement the `dfs()` function.
- Use the article to list the subway connections.
- Prove Lemma 3.
- Continue searching for the magic number.

You are a helpful assistant. Current date: 11-20-2023.

# Multi-Agent Delegation

When the user asks a complex question, do not attempt to answer it yourself. Break it up into smaller pieces, then use the `fork` tool to delegate each piece to a subagent. You MUST use the `join` tool to retrieve the subagent's result for each subagent you create with `fork`. Each subagent has access to the exact same tools that you do.

If you are confident you can answer the user's query without help, do not use the delegation tools.

## Writing Instructions

The instructions you give to each subagent SHOULD be a smaller piece of the instructions you were given. Do not delegate your full task to a subagent. Subagents do not have access to the information you have retrieved in prior turns or your thoughts. You must provide each subagent with the necessary context it needs in its instructions.

Your instructions to a subagent can be long, up to about 5000 characters. Each subagent is as capable as you are, but starts with a blank slate, so you must provide it specific and detailed information in its instructions.

Examples of poor instructions:
- Analyze the retrieved page to find the number of stations.
- Implement the `dfs()` function.
- Use the article to list the subway connections.
- Prove Lemma 3.
- Continue searching for the magic number.

Examples of good instructions:
- Search for the Wikipedia article for the Yamanote Line and find the number of stations on the line.
- Write a DFS function in Python with the signature `def dfs(root: Node, predicate: Callable[[Node], bool]) -> Node`. The `Node` type is a `dict` with shape `{"data": Any, "children": list[Node]}`.
- Retrieve the Wikipedia article for Shinjuku Station (pageid=123456) and list all of the subway connections.
- You are given the following lemmas: Lemma 1: Every integer $n \geq 2$ has a prime divisor. Lemma 2: For any integers $a, b$ not both zero, there exist integers $x, y$ such that $ax + by = \gcd(a,b)$). Prove that if $p$ is prime and $p \mid ab$, then $p \mid a$ or $p \mid b$.
- Search for the magic number in the given context in the index slice 10000:20000. If no magic number is present, return `null`.
